Waterfall method is when there is a sequence of discrete stages. One stage must be completed before moving on to the next one. At the end of each stage a deliverable is produced. At the end of each stage the project is reviewed and if a development error is found, a previous stage may have to be revisited or project may be restarted.

In Rapid Application Development (RAD) the project is subdivided into a series of builds. They are completed in parallel with their own separate timeframes. At the end the builds are assembled to create the finished project.

In waterfall, the end user is only involved at the analysis stage, but not again until implementation ✗, whereas in RAD, the end user is constantly involved with each individual build, throughout the entire project.
note: Quality of written communication assessed. Both methods are described and the answer finally compares user involvement, but the comparison is brief and the claim that waterfall users only return at implementation was marked wrong (users also sign off each stage), so it reaches the middle band.

An incremental backup is a copy of all data or software that has changed since the last backup of any kind (differential, incremental or full).
A full backup is a copy of all data on a system. It provides a full snapshot of the system at the time of backup.
To recover system, restore last full backup, then all incremental backups since then, in reverse order.
note: Quality of written communication assessed. Full marks for clearly describing both backup types and the recovery order. (Strictly, the incrementals are restored in the order they were made, oldest first.)
